claim: CRISPR technology has made generation of gene knock-outs widely achievable in cells.
source: CRISPR technology has made generation of gene knock-outs widely achievable in cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus about CRISPR technology capabilities.

claim: Once genes are inactivated, their re-activation remains difficult, especially in diploid cells.
source: However, once inactivated, their re-activation remains difficult, especially in diploid cells.
evidence: This statement describes a known limitation in the field based on established understanding.

claim: DExCon combines one-step CRISPR-Cas9-mediated targeted knockin of fluorescent proteins with an advanced Tet-inducible TRE3GS promoter.
source: Here, we present DExCon (Doxycycline-mediated endogenous gene Expression Control), DExogron (DExCon combined with auxin-mediated targeted protein degradation), and LUXon (light responsive DExCon) approaches which combine one-step CRISPR-Cas9-mediated targeted knockin of fluorescent proteins with an advanced Tet-inducible TRE3GS promoter.
evidence: This describes the experimental design and methodology developed in this study.

claim: DExCon, DExogron, and LUXon combine blockade of active gene expression with the ability to re-activate expression on demand.
source: These approaches combine blockade of active gene expression with the ability to re-activate expression on demand, including activation of silenced genes.
evidence: This describes the functional capabilities of the systems developed in this study.

claim: Systematic control can be exerted using doxycycline or spatiotemporally by light.
source: Systematic control can be exerted using doxycycline or spatiotemporally by light, and we demonstrate functional knock-out/rescue in the closely related Rab11 family of vesicle trafficking regulators.
evidence: This describes the control mechanisms demonstrated in the experimental work.

claim: Functional knock-out/rescue was demonstrated in the closely related Rab11 family of vesicle trafficking regulators.
source: Systematic control can be exerted using doxycycline or spatiotemporally by light, and we demonstrate functional knock-out/rescue in the closely related Rab11 family of vesicle trafficking regulators.
evidence: This describes experimental results demonstrating the functionality of the system.

claim: Fluorescent protein knock-in results in bright signals compatible with low-light live microscopy from monoallelic modification.
source: Fluorescent protein knock-in results in bright signals compatible with low-light live microscopy from monoallelic modification, the potential to simultaneously image different alleles of the same gene, and bypasses the need to work with clones.
evidence: This describes experimental observations about the imaging capabilities of the system.

claim: The system has the potential to simultaneously image different alleles of the same gene.
source: Fluorescent protein knock-in results in bright signals compatible with low-light live microscopy from monoallelic modification, the potential to simultaneously image different alleles of the same gene, and bypasses the need to work with clones.

evidence: This describes a practical advantage of the methodology.

claim: Protein levels are easily tunable to correspond with endogenous expression through cell sorting (DExCon).
source: Protein levels are easily tunable to correspond with endogenous expression through cell sorting (DExCon), timing of light illumination (LUXon), or by exposing cells to different levels of auxin (DExogron).

source: Furthermore, our approach allowed us to quantify previously unforeseen differences in vesicle dynamics, transferrin receptor recycling, expression kinetics, and protein stability among highly similar endogenous Rab11 family members and their colocalization in triple knock-in ovarian cancer cell lines.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 technology has revolutionized gene editing approaches.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 technology has revolutionized gene editing approaches and makes generation of gene knock-outs or knock-ins straightforward (Doudna and Charpentier, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 makes generation of gene knock-outs or knock-ins straightforward.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 technology has revolutionized gene editing approaches and makes generation of gene knock-outs or knock-ins straightforward (Doudna and Charpentier, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to established literature.

claim: Combination of CRISPR with single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) donors has proven to be the most precise and efficient method of on-target integration.
source: Combination of CRISPR with single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) donors has proven to be the most precise and efficient method of on-target integration (Quadros et al., 2017; Li et al., 2017), although knock-in approaches still suffer from low efficiencies, especially when aiming to achieve homozygosity (Gurumurthy et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Knock-in approaches still suffer from low efficiencies, especially when aiming to achieve homozygosity.
source: Combination of CRISPR with single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) donors has proven to be the most precise and efficient method of on-target integration (Quadros et al., 2017; Li et al., 2017), although knock-in approaches still suffer from low efficiencies, especially when aiming to achieve homozygosity (Gurumurthy et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Fluorescent protein (FP) knock-in at endogenous loci leading to protein-fusion allows functional enrichment of complete knock-in events.
source: Fluorescent protein (FP) knock-in at endogenous loci leading to protein-fusion allows functional enrichment of complete knock-in events and study of native protein function using fluorescent microscopy (Roberts et al., 2017; Leonetti et al., 2016).

claim: Fluorescent protein knock-in allows study of native protein function using fluorescent microscopy.

evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Fluorescent protein knock-ins only complement loss-of-function/gain-of-function methods.
source: However, they only complement loss-of-function/gain-of-function methods, and their usefulness is limited by brightness of the chosen FP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of existing methods.

claim: The usefulness of fluorescent protein knock-ins is limited by brightness of the chosen FP.
source: However, they only complement loss-of-function/gain-of-function methods, and their usefulness is limited by brightness of the chosen FP.
evidence: This is an inference based on known properties of fluorescent proteins.

claim: Conditional loss-of-function methods mainly rely on CRISPR/Cas9 combination with FLP-frt or Cre-LoxP systems.
source: Conditional loss-of-function methods mainly rely on CRISPR/Cas9 combination with FLP-frt or Cre-LoxP systems (Quadros et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: FLP-frt or Cre-LoxP systems are labor intensive and mediated by recombination, which is by nature irreversible.
source: However, these are labor intensive and mediated by recombination, which is by nature irreversible thus complicating attempts to rescue gene expression.

claim: The auxin-inducible degron (AID) system was introduced as a tag into the endogenous locus via CRISPR/Cas9.
source: Such levels of control can be partly offered by the auxin-inducible degron (AID) system (Nishimura et al., 2009) introduced as a tag into the endogenous locus via CRISPR/Cas9 (Röth et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: In the AID system, an exogenously expressed plant auxin receptor F-box protein triggers ubiquitylation and degradation of target proteins fused to an AID tag on addition of the plant hormone auxin.
source: Here, an exogenously expressed plant auxin receptor F-box protein triggers ubiquitylation and degradation of target proteins fused to an AID tag on addition of the plant hormone auxin.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of the AID system based on established knowledge.

claim: The AID system has limitations including poor spatial control due to diffusion of auxin.
source: However, this technology has its own limitations and caveats; for example, poor spatial control due to diffusion of auxin, significant basal degradation without auxin, and/or incomplete auxin-induced protein depletion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the properties of auxin as a small molecule.

claim: The AID system has significant basal degradation without auxin.
source: However, this technology has its own limitations and caveats; for example, poor spatial control due to diffusion of auxin, significant basal degradation without auxin, and/or incomplete auxin-induced protein depletion.
evidence: This is based on known limitations of the AID system.

claim: The AID system has incomplete auxin-induced protein depletion.
source: However, this technology has its own limitations and caveats; for example, poor spatial control due to diffusion of auxin, significant basal degradation without auxin, and/or incomplete auxin-induced protein depletion.
evidence: This is based on known limitations of the AID system.

claim: Rab11a, Rab11b, and Rab25 share high amino acid identity (Rab11a:Rab11b 89%, Rab11a:Rab25 66%, Rab11b:Rab25 61%).
source: Rab11s share high amino acid identity (Rab11a:Rab11b 89%, Rab11a:Rab25 66%, Rab11b:Rab25 61%), are known to play key roles in membrane transport, localize to recycling endosomes, and have been identified as important players in the cellular basis of an ever-increasing number of human disorders, including cell migration/invasion and cancer (Wilson et al., 2018; Kelly et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and supported by citations.

claim: Rab11 family members are known to play key roles in membrane transport.
source: Rab11s share high amino acid identity (Rab11a:Rab11b 89%, Rab11a:Rab25 66%, Rab11b:Rab25 61%), are known to play key roles in membrane transport, localize to recycling endosomes, and have been identified as important players in the cellular basis of an ever-increasing number of human disorders, including cell migration/invasion and cancer (Wilson et al., 2018; Kelly et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Rab11 family members localize to recycling endosomes.
source: Rab11s share high amino acid identity (Rab11a:Rab11b 89%, Rab11a:Rab25 66%, Rab11b:Rab25 61%), are known to play key roles in membrane transport, localize to recycling endosomes, and have been identified as important players in the cellular basis of an ever-increasing number of human disorders, including cell migration/invasion and cancer (Wilson et al., 2018; Kelly et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Rab11 family members have been identified as important players in the cellular basis of human disorders, including cell migration/invasion and cancer.
source: Rab11s share high amino acid identity (Rab11a:Rab11b 89%, Rab11a:Rab25 66%, Rab11b:Rab25 61%), are known to play key roles in membrane transport, localize to recycling endosomes, and have been identified as important players in the cellular basis of an ever-increasing number of human disorders, including cell migration/invasion and cancer (Wilson et al., 2018; Kelly et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Several Rab11 family isoforms have been reported.
source: Several Rab11 family isoforms have been reported (Ota et al., 2004), and specific antibodies are hard to obtain without cross-reactivity.
evidence: This is supported by citation to published research.

claim: Specific antibodies for Rab11 family members are hard to obtain without cross-reactivity.
source: Several Rab11 family isoforms have been reported (Ota et al., 2004), and specific antibodies are hard to obtain without cross-reactivity.
evidence: This is based on practical experience in the field.

claim: Much of what is known about Rab11 regulation and dynamics in live cells has been achieved with transiently transfected cDNA-mediated overexpression.
source: Moreover, much what is known about their regulation and dynamics in live cells has been achieved with the aid of transiently transfected cDNA (complementary DNA)-mediated overexpression which may lead to non-physiological artifacts (Ratz et al., 2015; Gibson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Transiently transfected cDNA-mediated overexpression may lead to non-physiological artifacts.
source: Moreover, much what is known about their regulation and dynamics in live cells has been achieved with the aid of transiently transfected cDNA (complementary DNA)-mediated overexpression which may lead to non-physiological artifacts (Ratz et al., 2015; Gibson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Rab11a, Rab11b, and Rab25 were significantly enriched in ovarian cancer, both for primary and recurrent tumors.
source: Rab11a, Rab11b, and Rab25 were significantly enriched in ovarian cancer, both for primary and recurrent tumors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Bioinformatic analyses suggested the existence of additional potentially protein-coding human Rab11a/b splice variants.
source: Bioinformatic analyses suggested the existence of additional potentially protein-coding human Rab11a/b splice variants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Analysis of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) revealed abundant expression of two Rab11b-coding and five Rab11a-coding transcripts across multiple healthy tissues.
source: Analysis of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) revealed abundant expression of two Rab11b-coding and five Rab11a-coding transcripts across multiple healthy tissues while Rab25 is more restricted, but expression is increased across multiple types of cancer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, https://doi.org/10.48420/16988617).
evidence: This is based on eQTL analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Rab25 expression is more restricted in healthy tissues but is increased across multiple types of cancer.
source: Analysis of expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) revealed abundant expression of two Rab11b-coding and five Rab11a-coding transcripts across multiple healthy tissues while Rab25 is more restricted, but expression is increased across multiple types of cancer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, https://doi.org/10.48420/16988617).
evidence: This is based on eQTL analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Several Rab11a/Rab11b/Rab25 splicing isoforms are enriched in ovarian cancer compared to normal tissue.
source: Similarly, several Rab11a/Rab11b/Rab25 splicing isoforms are enriched in ovarian cancer compared to normal tissue (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is based on analysis shown in the figure.

claim: All significantly expressed Rab11 transcripts share an intact N-terminus.
source: All significantly expressed transcripts share an intact N-terminus; however, for some splice variants, amino acids important for GTP/GDP binding (which allow oscillation between active/inactive states) or for the attachment to the outer leaflet of endosomal membranes are missing, which could therefore profoundly alter Rab11s function (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in the figure.

claim: For some Rab11 splice variants, amino acids important for GTP/GDP binding or for the attachment to the outer leaflet of endosomal membranes are missing.
source: All significantly expressed transcripts share an intact N-terminus; however, for some splice variants, amino acids important for GTP/GDP binding (which allow oscillation between active/inactive states) or for the attachment to the outer leaflet of endosomal membranes are missing, which could therefore profoundly alter Rab11s function (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in the figure.

claim: Missing amino acids important for GTP/GDP binding or membrane attachment could profoundly alter Rab11s function.
source: All significantly expressed transcripts share an intact N-terminus; however, for some splice variants, amino acids important for GTP/GDP binding (which allow oscillation between active/inactive states) or for the attachment to the outer leaflet of endosomal membranes are missing, which could therefore profoundly alter Rab11s function (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the known importance of these domains.

claim: Long ssDNA donor for precise and efficient on-target integration was used with flanking homologous arms 150–300 bases prepared via RNA intermediates.
source: We used long ssDNA donor for precise and efficient on-target integration (Quadros et al., 2017; Li et al., 2017; Miura et al., 2018) with flanking homologous arms 150–300 bases prepared via RNA intermediates (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, supported by citations.

claim: The optimized protocol combines magnetofection of long ssDNA and high fidelity (Hifi) Cas9 delivered as ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex with guideRNA (crRNA:tracrRNA).
source: Initial testing of different approaches led to our optimized protocol (Figure 1C) combining magnetofection of long ssDNA and high fidelity (Hifi) Cas9 delivered as ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complex with guideRNA (crRNA:tracrRNA).
evidence: This describes the optimized methodology developed in the study.

claim: The combination of magnetofection and Hifi Cas9 RNP reduces off-target effects to non-detectable levels and leads to Hifi hetero/homozygous knockin.
source: This combination reduces off-target effects to non-detectable levels and leads to Hifi hetero/homozygous knockin (Vakulskas et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes experimental results supported by citation.

claim: Pilot testing led to a high rate of successful knock-in in HEK293T cells with expected localization of Rab11a (10–20%) or Rab11b (2–10%).
source: Pilot testing led to a high rate of successful knock-in human embryonic kidney (HEK)293T cells with expected localization of Rab11a (10–20%) or Rab11b (2–10%), respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This describes experimental results from pilot testing.

claim: Integration of mNeonGreen or mCherry after the start codon of Rab11a or Rab11b in A2780 cells was less efficient (0.2–1%) compared to HEK293T.
source: For further work, we selected a commonly used cell line model for ovarian cancer, A2780, and knocked-in mNeonGreen or mCherry after the start codon of Rab11a or Rab11b, respectively (Figure 1D). This integration, although less efficient (0.2–1%) compared to HEK293T, was specific as all sorted cells exhibited correct Rab11a/b localization, and our protocol was also successful in a second ovarian cancer cell line that has defective homologous recombination (BRCA-1 mutant COV362 Beaufort et al., 2014; Figure 1E).
evidence: This describes experimental results comparing efficiency across cell lines.

claim: All sorted A2780 cells exhibited correct Rab11a/b localization.
source: This integration, although less efficient (0.2–1%) compared to HEK293T, was specific as all sorted cells exhibited correct Rab11a/b localization, and our protocol was also successful in a second ovarian cancer cell line that has defective homologous recombination (BRCA-1 mutant COV362 Beaufort et al., 2014; Figure 1E).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: The protocol was successful in a second ovarian cancer cell line that has defective homologous recombination (BRCA-1 mutant COV362).
source: This integration, although less efficient (0.2–1%) compared to HEK293T, was specific as all sorted cells exhibited correct Rab11a/b localization, and our protocol was also successful in a second ovarian cancer cell line that has defective homologous recombination (BRCA-1 mutant COV362 Beaufort et al., 2014; Figure 1E).
evidence: This describes experimental results supported by citation.

claim: Western blotting with antibodies that recognize Rab11a, or both Rab11a and Rab11b, confirmed knock-in.
source: Western blotting with antibodies that recognize Rab11a, or both Rab11a and Rab11b, confirmed knock-in (Figure 1F).
evidence: This describes experimental validation by western blot.

claim: A proportion of cells showed truncation of the linker flanking the FP but not in the integrated homologous arms.
source: Consistent with the literature (Li et al., 2017; Canaj et al., 2019), a proportion of cells showed truncation of the linker flanking the FP (Figure 1G) but not in the integrated homologous arms, indicating that sorting cells for fluorescence (or another functional protein) is important for establishing in frame knock-in at the N-terminus preserving protein function.
evidence: This describes experimental observations supported by citations.

claim: Sorting cells for fluorescence is important for establishing in frame knock-in at the N-terminus preserving protein function.
source: Consistent with the literature (Li et al., 2017; Canaj et al., 2019), a proportion of cells showed truncation of the linker flanking the FP (Figure 1G) but not in the integrated homologous arms, indicating that sorting cells for fluorescence (or another functional protein) is important for establishing in frame knock-in at the N-terminus preserving protein function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of truncations.

claim: Integration of the antiGFPnanobody sequence was not complete in ~90% of mCherry-positive cells.
source: Although knock-in to the Rab11a locus showed the expected localization of mCherry-Rab11a in all sorted cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), integration of the antiGFPnanobody sequence was not complete in ~90% of mCherry-positive cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B-C).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: The TRE3GS promoter lacks binding sites for endogenous mammalian transcription factors.
source: This promoter lacks binding sites for endogenous mammalian transcription factors, is effectively silent in the absence of induction, and any transcription driven by endogenous active promoter generates non-sense frameshift.
evidence: This describes the properties of the TRE3GS promoter based on its design.

claim: The TRE3GS promoter is effectively silent in the absence of induction.
source: This promoter lacks binding sites for endogenous mammalian transcription factors, is effectively silent in the absence of induction, and any transcription driven by endogenous active promoter generates non-sense frameshift.
evidence: This describes the properties of the TRE3GS promoter based on its design.

claim: Any transcription driven by endogenous active promoter in the DExCon system generates non-sense frameshift.
source: This promoter lacks binding sites for endogenous mammalian transcription factors, is effectively silent in the absence of induction, and any transcription driven by endogenous active promoter generates non-sense frameshift.
evidence: This describes the design feature of the DExCon system.

claim: Sorted DExCon cells showed expression of corresponding FP-Rab11 with a perinuclear vesicle-enriched localization matching the endogenous protein, but only in the presence of dox.
source: Sorted cells showed expression of corresponding FP-Rab11 with a perinuclear vesicle-enriched localization matching the endogenous protein, but only in the presence of dox, and decreased levels of non-modified endogenous Rab11a/b indicating that DExCon blocks expression at the endogenous locus (Figure 2B and C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: DExCon blocks expression at the endogenous locus as indicated by decreased levels of non-modified endogenous Rab11a/b.
source: Sorted cells showed expression of corresponding FP-Rab11 with a perinuclear vesicle-enriched localization matching the endogenous protein, but only in the presence of dox, and decreased levels of non-modified endogenous Rab11a/b indicating that DExCon blocks expression at the endogenous locus (Figure 2B and C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: The main Rab11b protein-coding splice variant 201 is ~4× more abundant than the protein-coding splice variant 202.
source: The main Rab11b protein-coding splice variant 201 is ~4× more abundant than the protein-coding splice variant 202, consistent with eQTLs analysis of ovarian cancer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), and DExCon modification did not significantly influence their relative abundance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on qPCR analysis shown in the figure.

claim: DExCon modification did not significantly influence the relative abundance of Rab11b splice variants 201 and 202.
source: The main Rab11b protein-coding splice variant 201 is ~4× more abundant than the protein-coding splice variant 202, consistent with eQTLs analysis of ovarian cancer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), and DExCon modification did not significantly influence their relative abundance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on qPCR analysis shown in the figure.

claim: The DExCon module did not change the ratio of Rab11b splice variants 201/202/204 upon dox induction.
source: Specific primers that detect splice variants 201, 202, and a third (short and likely untranslated) 204 variant indicated that the latter is expressed, but again the DExCon module did not change the ratio of Rab11b splice variants 201/202/204 upon dox induction.
evidence: This is based on qPCR analysis.

claim: The DExCon module can recapitulate the spectrum of splice variant expression from the Rab11b locus.
source: This suggests that the DExCon module can recapitulate the spectrum of splice variant expression from the Rab11b locus and provides an advantage over generation of a knock-out cell line and subsequent tet-inducible protein-coding rescue from a viral vector containing cDNA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the qPCR data showing preserved splice variant ratios.

claim: In all combinations of double knock-in, endogenous Rab11a/Rab11b localization driven by dox-induced or endogenous promoter was significantly correlated.
source: In all combinations, endogenous Rab11a/Rab11b localization driven by dox-induced or endogenous promoter was significantly correlated, and both Rab11a and Rab11b concentrated in vesicles at the perinuclear recycling compartment (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is based on imaging and colocalization analysis.

claim: Both Rab11a and Rab11b concentrated in vesicles at the perinuclear recycling compartment.
source: In all combinations, endogenous Rab11a/Rab11b localization driven by dox-induced or endogenous promoter was significantly correlated, and both Rab11a and Rab11b concentrated in vesicles at the perinuclear recycling compartment (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: This is based on imaging observations.

claim: Transient transfection of plasmids coding FP-Rab11a/Rab11b gave very bright overlapping signals, but large vesicles were observed particularly toward the cell periphery.
source: By contrast, transient transfection of plasmids coding FP-Rab11a/Rab11b gave very bright overlapping signals, but large vesicles were observed particularly toward the cell periphery (Figure 2G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations comparing transfection to knock-in.

claim: DExCon can induce expression from the endogenous gene locus that preserves physiological distribution of the protein within cells with signal intensities compatible with low light/exposure live microscopy.
source: These findings were confirmed when red/green-FPs were switched (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B) and suggest that DExCon can induce expression from the endogenous gene locus that preserves physiological distribution of the protein within cells with signal intensities compatible with low light/exposure live microscopy (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C,D; Videos 1–2).
evidence: This is an inference based on imaging observations.

claim: While Rab11a vesicle intensity is consistent within polarized cells, Rab11b intensity is increased at the tips of protrusions relative to the region of the cell in front of the nucleus.
source: However, DExCon knock-ins showed higher intensity and could therefore be visualized at lower exposure, avoiding caveats associated with lag (mis-localization) and photobleaching, revealing that while Rab11a vesicle intensity is consistent within polarized cells, Rab11b intensity is increased at the tips of protrusions relative to the region of the cell in front of the nucleus (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is based on quantitative imaging analysis in 3D environments.

claim: Encoding functionality at each of the 5′ and 3′ ends of ssDNA donor allows enrichment of accurately modified cells even for non-fluorescent coding genes.
source: Upon dox induction, all sorted cells exhibited the expected localization of Rab11a or Rab11b (Figure 2H) and full-length size on western blot (Figure 2I) indicating that encoding functionality at each of the 5′ and 3′ ends of ssDNA donor allows enrichment of accurately modified cells even for non-fluorescent coding genes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful knock-in of GFP nanobody-mCherry.

claim: A2780 ovarian cancer cells show abundant Rab11a/b expression while the more restricted family member Rab25 is not expressed.
source: A2780 ovarian cancer cells show abundant Rab11a/b expression while the more restricted family member Rab25 is not expressed (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on western blot analysis.

claim: Dox treatment of Rab25 DExCon cells led to mNeonGreen fluorescence with expected perinuclear localization of mNeonGreen-Rab25 in all sorted cells.
source: TRE3GS-mNeonGreen was delivered by long ssDNA-mediated knock-in to the Rab25 locus in A2780 cells expressing Tet-On 3G transactivator. Dox treatment led to mNeonGreen fluorescence with expected perinuclear localization of mNeonGreen-Rab25 in all sorted cells (in 2D and 3D-CDM; Figure 3C) and specificity of integration was confirmed by western blot (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) and sequencing (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Exposing cells to different dox concentrations appeared to have a dose-dependent effect when analyzed by western blotting.
source: We next explored tunability of Rab25 expression. Exposing cells to different dox concentrations appeared to have a dose-dependent effect when analyzed by western blotting (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C); however, fluorescence microscopy revealed that the difference was primarily due to the number of responding cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Fluorescence microscopy revealed that the difference in dox response was primarily due to the number of responding cells.
source: We next explored tunability of Rab25 expression. Exposing cells to different dox concentrations appeared to have a dose-dependent effect when analyzed by western blotting (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C); however, fluorescence microscopy revealed that the difference was primarily due to the number of responding cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: There is a positive correlation between expression of Tet-On 3G transactivator and mNeonGreen-Rab25.
source: Nevertheless, we noticed a positive correlation between expression of Tet-On 3G transactivator, reported as mTagBFP fluorescence, and mNeonGreen-Rab25 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D; R=0.43, p=0.0003).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Dox-induced Rab25 expression levels in 'low' sorted cells were comparable to endogenous Rab25 expression levels in OVCAR-3 ovarian cancer cell lines over 48 hr.
source: Dox-induced Rab25 expression levels in 'low' sorted cells were comparable to endogenous Rab25 expression levels in OVCAR-3 ovarian cancer cell lines over 48 hr (Figure 3E) and Rab25 expression levels correlated with Tet-On 3G levels as expected (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is based on western blot comparison.

claim: The ability to re-induce previously sorted expression levels was preserved over several months under standard cell culture conditions and reached maximal fluorescence after 72 hr.
source: The ability to re-induce previously sorted expression levels was preserved over several months under standard cell culture conditions and reached maximal fluorescence after 72 hr (Figure 3E).
evidence: This describes experimental observations over time.

claim: The DExCon approach was able to re-activate endogenous silenced Rab25 on demand and levels could be tuned to match endogenous, physiologically relevant expression levels.
source: These results indicate that the DExCon approach was able to re-activate endogenous silenced Rab25 on demand and levels could be tuned to match endogenous, physiologically relevant expression levels.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Cells stably expressing PA-Tet-ON2, PA-Tet-OFF1, or two showed the expected Rab25 endosomal localization after being illuminated by blue light for 24 hr and sorted.
source: Cells stably expressing PA-Tet-ON2, PA-Tet-OFF1, or two were then edited by mNeonGreen DExCon knock-in to the Rab25 locus, illuminated by blue light for 24 hr and sorted, all showing the expected Rab25 endosomal localization (Figure 3H; Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Cyclical exposure to light/dark led to repeatable re-silencing of Rab25.
source: Cyclical exposure to light/dark led to repeatable re-silencing of Rab25, and the level of re-activation could be modulated by timing of blue light which is one of the major advantages of a light-inducible gene expression system (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: The level of Rab25 re-activation could be modulated by timing of blue light.
source: Cyclical exposure to light/dark led to repeatable re-silencing of Rab25, and the level of re-activation could be modulated by timing of blue light which is one of the major advantages of a light-inducible gene expression system (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Dox addition with blue light was necessary to re-activate Rab25 in PA-Tet-ON2 system.
source: Dox addition with blue light was necessary to re-activate Rab25 in PA-Tet-ON2 system (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), while dox addition to PA-Tet-OFF1/2 completely blocked expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Dox addition to PA-Tet-OFF1/2 completely blocked Rab25 expression.
source: Dox addition with blue light was necessary to re-activate Rab25 in PA-Tet-ON2 system (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E), while dox addition to PA-Tet-OFF1/2 completely blocked expression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Some Rab25 positive vesicles in close proximity of the nucleus were significantly less mobile compared to others.
source: Interestingly, in addition to the expected Rab25 localization, we observed some Rab25 positive vesicles in close proximity of the nucleus. These vesicles were significantly less mobile compared to others suggesting that the nucleus could under some circumstances sterically block movement of vesicles (Figure 3H; Videos 5 and 6).
evidence: This is based on live imaging observations.

claim: The nucleus could under some circumstances sterically block movement of vesicles.
source: Interestingly, in addition to the expected Rab25 localization, we observed some Rab25 positive vesicles in close proximity of the nucleus. These vesicles were significantly less mobile compared to others suggesting that the nucleus could under some circumstances sterically block movement of vesicles (Figure 3H; Videos 5 and 6).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation of less mobile vesicles near the nucleus.

claim: Longer exposure to blue light led to brighter mNeonGreen signal in both PA-Tet-OFF/ON systems with expected Rab25 localization in polarized/elongated cells interacting with matrix fibrils.
source: Longer exposure to blue light led to brighter mNeonGreen signal in both PA-Tet-OFF/ON systems with expected Rab25 localization in polarized/elongated cells interacting with matrix fibrils (Figure 3K; Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: There was a significant dose-dependent effect of Rab25 induction via light exposure for over 6 hr on invasion.
source: When all cells were pre-illuminated 2 days before invasion to induce Rab25 expression, we saw a significant dose-dependent effect of Rab25 induction via light exposure for over 6 hr on invasion that was not observed in the presence of dox in the TET-OFF system (Figure 3L–N).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of spheroid invasion assays.

claim: Tight control of gene expression levels and their impact on complex cell behavior can be easily achieved/studied by the LUXon system.
source: This demonstrates that tight control of gene expression levels and their impact on complex cell behavior can be easily achieved/studied by the LUXon system.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Activation of Rab25 expression increased the localization of Rab11a and Rab11b at ERC spots.
source: Interestingly, activation of Rab25 expression increased the localization of Rab11a and Rab11b at ERC spots, suggesting that Rab11a/b/25 networks are interconnected and can be modulated by Rab25 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), consistent with redistribution of Rab11a in Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cells upon the introduction of Rab25 expression (Casanova et al., 1999).
evidence: This is based on imaging observations.

claim: Rab11a/b/25 networks are interconnected and can be modulated by Rab25 expression.
source: Interestingly, activation of Rab25 expression increased the localization of Rab11a and Rab11b at ERC spots, suggesting that Rab11a/b/25 networks are interconnected and can be modulated by Rab25 expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), consistent with redistribution of Rab11a in Madin-Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cells upon the introduction of Rab25 expression (Casanova et al., 1999).
evidence: This is an inference based on imaging observations and supported by citation.

claim: While there was clear colocalization between Rab11a/b/25 and TFN, some vesicles were highly enriched for Rab25 compared to Rab11a/b but lacked TFN.
source: While there was clear colocalization between Rab11a/b/25 and TFN, some vesicles were highly enriched for Rab25 compared to Rab11a/b but lacked TFN.
evidence: This is based on imaging observations.

claim: Rab25 enriched vesicles negative for TFN were found in close proximity to the nucleus in ∼90% of triple knock-in cells.
source: Rab25 enriched vesicles negative for TFN were found in close proximity to the nucleus in ∼90% of triple knock-in cells (Figure 4B), both in 2D and 3D environments (Figure 4C; Videos 9–12).
evidence: This is based on imaging observations.

claim: There is no significant difference in TFN colocalization with Rab11 family members.
source: This analysis revealed that there is no significant difference in TFN colocalization with Rab11 family members, but Rab11a colocalizes with Rab11b to a significantly higher extent than with Rab25, or Rab11b with Rab25 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is based on quantitative colocalization analysis.

claim: Rab11a colocalizes with Rab11b to a significantly higher extent than with Rab25, or Rab11b with Rab25.
source: This analysis revealed that there is no significant difference in TFN colocalization with Rab11 family members, but Rab11a colocalizes with Rab11b to a significantly higher extent than with Rab25, or Rab11b with Rab25 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is based on quantitative colocalization analysis.

claim: 16.1% of all Rab11 vesicles/26.5% of TFN vesicles show Rab11a/b/25 largely colocalizing with TFN, one another, or all at the same time.
source: Rab11a/b/25 largely colocalize with TFN, one another, or all at the same time (16.1% of all Rab11 vesicles/26.5% of TFN vesicles; Figure 4E) and that differences between Rab11 family members are mainly due to the unique Rab25 recruitment to a subset of vesicles (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is based on quantitative colocalization analysis.

claim: Differences between Rab11 family members are mainly due to the unique Rab25 recruitment to a subset of vesicles.
source: Rab11a/b/25 largely colocalize with TFN, one another, or all at the same time (16.1% of all Rab11 vesicles/26.5% of TFN vesicles; Figure 4E) and that differences between Rab11 family members are mainly due to the unique Rab25 recruitment to a subset of vesicles (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the colocalization analysis.

claim: mNeonGreen-Rab11a DExCon reached ~75% of its maximal expression peak at 24 hr, significantly faster than other family members.
source: mNeonGreen-Rab11a DExCon reached ~75% of its maximal expression peak at 24 hr, significantly faster than other family members: at 24 hr mCherry-Rab11b DExCon reached ~50% peak expression, whereas mNeonGreen-Rab25 DExCon only reached ~40% (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of expression kinetics.

claim: At 24 hr mCherry-Rab11b DExCon reached ~50% peak expression.
source: mNeonGreen-Rab11a DExCon reached ~75% of its maximal expression peak at 24 hr, significantly faster than other family members: at 24 hr mCherry-Rab11b DExCon reached ~50% peak expression, whereas mNeonGreen-Rab25 DExCon only reached ~40% (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of expression kinetics.

claim: At 24 hr mNeonGreen-Rab25 DExCon only reached ~40% peak expression.
source: mNeonGreen-Rab11a DExCon reached ~75% of its maximal expression peak at 24 hr, significantly faster than other family members: at 24 hr mCherry-Rab11b DExCon reached ~50% peak expression, whereas mNeonGreen-Rab25 DExCon only reached ~40% (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of expression kinetics.

claim: There is an inverse relationship between methylation of the Rab25 promoter and its expression, where decreased methylation is correlated with increased gene expression, at both mRNA and protein levels across all cancer types.
source: We found that there is an inverse relationship between methylation of the Rab25 promoter and its expression, where decreased methylation is correlated with increased gene expression, at both mRNA and protein levels across all cancer types (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis.

claim: The chromatin structure of the silenced Rab25 locus, both in promoter and enhancer sequences, is less accessible for transcriptional machinery to drive transcription.
source: ATAC-seq dataset analysis further suggested that the chromatin structure of the silenced Rab25 locus, both in promoter and enhancer sequences, is less accessible for transcriptional machinery to drive transcription (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on ATAC-seq analysis.

claim: In OVCAR-3 cells where both Rab11a and Rab25 are endogenously expressed, there was no delay in the normalized expression kinetics of Rab25.
source: Dox induction again led to the correct localization of Rab11a or Rab25, as expected (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), but this time there was no delay in the normalized expression kinetics of Rab25, as was observed for A2780 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on comparison of expression kinetics between cell lines.

claim: In both A2780 and OVCAR-3 cells Rab11a DExCon always led to greater fluorescence intensity compared to Rab25 DExCon.
source: Interestingly, in both A2780 and OVCAR-3 cells Rab11a DExCon always led to greater fluorescence intensity compared to Rab25 DExCon, suggesting additional mechanisms of protein level control (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is based on comparison of fluorescence intensity.

claim: Expression kinetics of double DExCon-mCherry/DExCon-mNeonGreen Rab11b cells were noticeably different between mCherry and mNeonGreen modified Rab11b.
source: Unexpectedly, expression kinetics of double DExCon-mCherry/DExCon-mNeonGreen Rab11b cells were noticeably different between mCherry and mNeonGreen modified Rab11b (Figure 5H; Video 13).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of expression kinetics.

claim: mCherry-Rab11b showed remarkably stable fluorescence, whereas mNeonGreen-Rab11b was lost more rapidly.
source: When DExCon cells were pre-induced with dox for 24 hr, followed by dox removal, a decrease in fluorescence was observed over time (Figure 5I). mCherry-Rab11b showed remarkably stable fluorescence, whereas mNeonGreen-Rab11b was lost more rapidly.
evidence: This is based on analysis of protein stability after dox removal.

claim: mNeonGreen fluorescence continuously declined overtime, where Rab11a and Rab11b decreased in intensity more rapidly than Rab25 following dox removal.
source: By contrast, mNeonGreen fluorescence continuously declined overtime, where Rab11a and Rab11b decreased in intensity more rapidly than Rab25 following dox removal (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is based on analysis of protein stability after dox removal.

claim: The FP is an important consideration when using FP-knock-in to understand protein dynamics.
source: This suggests that the FP is an important consideration when using FP-knock-in to understand protein dynamics but opens the possibility of modifying individual (e.g. mutant vs non-mutant) alleles within cells to study their stability and function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed differences in stability between mCherry and mNeonGreen.

claim: Direct comparison of Rab11a/b/25 dynamics revealed an ultra-fast relocalization of Rab11a (t1/2=209 s), significantly slower Rab11b relocalization (t1/2=362 s), and slower still dynamics of Rab25 (t1/2=476 s).
source: Direct comparison of Rab11a/b/25 dynamics revealed an ultra-fast relocalization of Rab11a (t1/2=209 s), significantly slower Rab11b relocalization (t1/2=362 s), and slower still dynamics of Rab25 (t1/2=476 s) (Figure 5M; Figure 5—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of knocksideways experiments.

claim: Dox treatment led to rescue of protein expression as expected and simultaneous addition of IAA efficiently depleted dox-induced expression only when the degron tag was present (DExogron minilAA7-mCherry-Rab11b).
source: Dox treatment led to rescue of protein expression as expected and simultaneous addition of Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA as a source of auxin) efficiently depleted dox-induced expression only when the degron tag was present (DExogron minilAA7-mCherry-Rab11b) (Figure 6C; Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, F; Videos 14 and 15).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: IAA/dox co-treatment (24–48 hr) decreases DExogron-mCherry-Rab11b fluorescence to the level of un-treated Rab11b miniIAA7-mCherry knock-in cells with degradation half time kinetics of 1.7±0.1 hr.
source: Flow cytometry analysis confirmed that IAA/dox co-treatment (24–48 hr) decreases DExogron-mCherry-Rab11b fluorescence to the level of un-treated Rab11b miniIAA7-mCherry knock-in cells with degradation half time kinetics of 1.7±0.1 hr (Figure 6D and E; Figure 6—figure supplement 1G; Video 14).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry and kinetic analysis.

claim: Introducing a degron tag using one donor without additional DExCon modification led to a decrease in mCherry fluorescence.
source: Introducing a degron tag using one donor without additional DExCon modification led to a decrease in mCherry fluorescence (Figure 6D) and revealed two additional drawbacks.
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: A significant proportion of cells did not respond to IAA likely due to the truncation of the minilAA7 sequence during HDR.
source: A significant proportion of cells did not respond to IAA likely due to the truncation of the minilAA7 sequence during HDR (Figure 6—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of non-responsive cells.

claim: Treatment with IAA resulted in 90–70% mCherry removal, which was close to the control level but not complete.
source: However, treatment with IAA resulted in 90–70% mCherry removal, which was close to the control level but not complete, limiting the effectiveness as complete removal tool (Figure 6D).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Rab11a or Rab11b DExCon or DExogron modified cells closes the wound significantly later than control wt cells in the absence of dox-induced expression.
source: To test the functionality of DExCons/DExogrons, we performed a 2D scratch wound migration assay and found that Rab11a or Rab11b DExCon or DExogron modified cells closes the wound significantly later than control wt cells in the absence of dox-induced expression, and this phenotype is further amplified by Rab11a/b knock-out combinations (Figure 6F; Figure 6—figure supplement 2A; Video 16).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of wound healing assays.

claim: Knock-out phenotypes were reversed when Rab11a/b expression was re-activated with dox.
source: Knock-out phenotypes were reversed when Rab11a/b expression was re-activated with dox; however, induction of degradation with IAA did not oppose this rescue, suggesting that IAA induced Rab11b depletion is incomplete in the presence of dox and is not sufficient to mimic the knock-out phenotype.
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: IAA induced Rab11b depletion is incomplete in the presence of dox and is not sufficient to mimic the knock-out phenotype.
source: Knock-out phenotypes were reversed when Rab11a/b expression was re-activated with dox; however, induction of degradation with IAA did not oppose this rescue, suggesting that IAA induced Rab11b depletion is incomplete in the presence of dox and is not sufficient to mimic the knock-out phenotype.
evidence: This is an inference based on the inability of IAA to reverse the rescue.

claim: Any change in Rab11a/b expression did not alter cell growth.
source: The effect of proliferation on wound healing closure was negligible, as any change in Rab11a/b expression did not alter cell growth (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is based on proliferation assays.

claim: A toxic effect of IAA (100 μg/ml) was observed from 10 hr of exposure when A2780 cells seeded sparsely.
source: Notably, we observed a toxic effect of IAA (100 μg/ml) from 10 hr of exposure when A2780 cells seeded sparsely.
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Reducing Rab11a or b expression using shRNA, DExCon, DExogron, or their combination decreased the ability of cells/spheroids to invade FN-rich collagen.
source: To investigate how manipulation of Rab11a/b expression influences cell migration/invasion into 3D collagen/FN matrix, we performed spheroid invasion assays. Reducing Rab11a or b expression using shRNA, DExCon, DExogron, or their combination decreased the ability of cells/spheroids to invade FN-rich collagen, and this was significantly rescued by dox treatment in Rab11a DExCon single knock-in cells (Figure 6G; Figure 6—figure supplement 2D,E).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of spheroid invasion assays.

claim: Dox-induced re-expression of Rab11b had a dose-dependent dominant-negative effect on invasion under all combinations, sufficiently blocking even Rab11a rescue.
source: Dox-induced re-expression of Rab11b had a dose-dependent dominant-negative effect on invasion under all combinations, sufficiently blocking even Rab11a rescue.
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: The negative effect of Rab11b rescue was reversed by simultaneous dox/IAA co-treatment and led to cell invasion comparable to wt control cells or even significantly higher.
source: The negative effect of Rab11b rescue was reversed by simultaneous dox/IAA co-treatment and led to cell invasion comparable to wt control cells or even significantly higher (Figure 6H–I) despite the cytotoxic effect of IAA observed on individually migrating cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D,E vs Figure 6H).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Cells are sensitive to Rab11b re-expression levels and that balanced dosage is needed for coordination of membrane trafficking important for 3D cell migration.
source: This confirms Rab11b functionality and suggests that cells are sensitive to Rab11b re-expression levels and that balanced dosage is needed for coordination of membrane trafficking important for 3D cell migration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the dose-dependent effects observed.

claim: mCherry fluorescence intensity of DExogron Rab11b cells or DExogron-Rab11b/DExCon-Rab11a cells was slightly, but significantly, decreased below the fluorescence of dox/IAA co-treated cells as early as 1–4 hr after switching to dox-free media supplemented only with IAA.
source: We next tested whether induction of degradation with IAA can improve the AID pitfall of incomplete Rab11b depletion by withdrawing dox following re-activation of Rab11b expression. Indeed, mCherry fluorescence intensity of DExogron Rab11b cells or DExogron-Rab11b/DExCon-Rab11a cells was slightly, but significantly, decreased below the fluorescence of dox/IAA co-treated cells as early as 1–4 hr after switching to dox-free media supplemented only with IAA (Figure 6J; Figure 6—figure supplement 3A) and returned to non-detectable levels in 24–48 hr (Figure 6K).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: The DExogron is an important modification that can lead to complete removal of protein following withdrawal of dox-induced gene expression.
source: These data show that the DExogron is an important modification that can lead to complete removal of protein following withdrawal of dox-induced gene expression.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Degradation was significantly slowed but still occurred to a similar extent when IAA concentration was dropped from 100 µg/ml to 0.5 µg/ml up to 2.5 µg/ml.
source: Because IAA appeared to influence cell proliferation, we dropped its concentration from 100 µg/ml to 0.5 µg/ml and found that degradation was significantly slowed but still occurred to a similar extent up to 2.5 µg/ml (Figure 6K and L; Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Dox/IAA co-treatment was sufficient to tune DExogron mCherry-Rab11b to endogenous levels (IAA 0.5 µg/ml).
source: Dox/IAA co-treatment was sufficient to tune DExogron mCherry-Rab11b to endogenous levels (IAA 0.5 µg/ml; Figure 6L).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: DExogron-Rab11a/DExCon-Rab11b resulted in tuned steady-state fluorescence intensity of mNeonGreen Rab11a with degradation halftime kinetics around 2.5±0.1 hr.
source: DExogron-Rab11a/DExCon-Rab11b similarly resulted in tuned steady-state fluorescence intensity of mNeonGreen Rab11a with degradation halftime kinetics around 2.5±0.1 hr (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A-E; Video 17).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: DExogron can eliminate the shortcomings of the AID system, allowing fine-tuning of expression levels up to complete depletion following CRISPR-based modification.
source: These data therefore indicate that DExogron can eliminate the shortcomings of the AID system, allowing fine-tuning of expression levels up to complete depletion following CRISPR-based modification.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Although Rab11b and Rab11a may have a complementary function in migration and invasion of A2780 ovarian cancer cells, they differ substantially in their post-transcriptional regulation.
source: Furthermore, our results suggest that although Rab11b and Rab11a may have a complementary function in migration and invasion of A2780 ovarian cancer cells, they differ substantially in their post-transcriptional regulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed differences in expression kinetics and stability.

claim: Recycling of TFN-R is typically biphasic with an initial rapid direct route from early endosomes to the plasma membrane (under control of Rab4) and a slower non-essential route that requires additional trafficking through perinuclear recycling endosomes via Rab11.
source: Recycling of TFN-R is typically biphasic with an initial rapid direct route from early endosomes to the plasma membrane (under control of Rab4) and a slower non-essential route that requires additional trafficking through perinuclear recycling endosomes via Rab11 (Daro et al., 1996; Sheff et al., 2002; Sheff et al., 1999; Figure 7A).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: DExCon or DExogron modified Rab11a or Rab11b cells which lack expression of the targeted GTPase(s) had little impact on TFN-R recycling at 30 min.
source: DExCon or DExogron modified Rab11a or Rab11b cells which lack expression of the targeted GTPase(s) had little impact on TFN-R recycling at 30 min (Figure 7B), suggesting that fast recycling is likely predominant in A2780 cells as in other cell types (Sheff et al., 1999).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Fast recycling is likely predominant in A2780 cells as in other cell types.
source: DExCon or DExogron modified Rab11a or Rab11b cells which lack expression of the targeted GTPase(s) had little impact on TFN-R recycling at 30 min (Figure 7B), suggesting that fast recycling is likely predominant in A2780 cells as in other cell types (Sheff et al., 1999).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations and supported by citation.

claim: Re-expression of Rab25 did not impact upon recycling, indicating that this Rab11 family member may have a limited influence on trafficking this cargo.
source: Re-expression of Rab25 did not impact upon recycling, indicating that this Rab11 family member may have a limited influence on trafficking this cargo (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: Dox-induced high-level expression of either Rab11a or Rab11b under DExCon/DExogron control decreased the level of recycling at 30 min.
source: However, dox-induced high-level expression of either Rab11a or Rab11b under DExCon/DExogron control decreased the level of recycling at 30 min (Figure 7B), consistent with the literature (Ren et al., 1998), perhaps by favoring the slow-recycling route.
evidence: This describes experimental observations supported by citation.

claim: High-level expression of Rab11a or Rab11b may favor the slow-recycling route.
source: However, dox-induced high-level expression of either Rab11a or Rab11b under DExCon/DExogron control decreased the level of recycling at 30 min (Figure 7B), consistent with the literature (Ren et al., 1998), perhaps by favoring the slow-recycling route.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: DExCon/DExogron Rab11a/b cells selected for expression levels comparable to endogenous Rab11a/b knock-in did not have any significant effect on TFN-R recycling rate compared to the non-modified control.
source: DExCon/DExogron Rab11a/b cells selected for expression levels comparable to endogenous Rab11a/b knock-in did not have any significant effect on TFN-R recycling rate compared to the non-modified control, indicating that it is the expression level that slows recycling.
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: It is the expression level of Rab11a/b that slows recycling.
source: DExCon/DExogron Rab11a/b cells selected for expression levels comparable to endogenous Rab11a/b knock-in did not have any significant effect on TFN-R recycling rate compared to the non-modified control, indicating that it is the expression level that slows recycling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of different expression levels.

claim: IAA/Dox co-treatment of DExogron-Rab11b cells led to near-physiological levels of Rab11b which had no significant effect on TFN-R recycling.
source: Similarly, IAA/Dox co-treatment of DExogron-Rab11b cells led to near-physiological levels of Rab11b which had no significant effect on TFN-R recycling (Figure 7B).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: TFN-R recycling slowed by high Rab11a DExCon levels was restored to the level of double knock-out cells by lowering Rab11b levels with DExogron (Rab11a DExCon/Rab11b DExogron, IAA/dox co-treatment).
source: Surprisingly, TFN-R recycling slowed by high Rab11a DExCon levels was restored to the level of double knock-out cells by lowering Rab11b levels with DExogron (Rab11a DExCon/Rab11b DExogron, IAA/dox co-treatment).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Rab11a/Rab11b can recycle TFN-R via the slow recycling pathway, and increasing levels of Rab11a/b could favor the slow-recycling route to delay recycling of TFN.
source: These data suggest that Rab11a/Rab11b can recycle TFN-R via the slow recycling pathway, and that increasing levels of Rab11a/b could favor the slow-recycling route to delay recycling of TFN.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: Cells induced to have high-level expression of DExCon-mNeonGreen-Rab11a or/and DExogron-mCherry-Rab11b showed lower levels of TFN-R recycling compared to control.
source: Cells induced to have high-level expression of DExCon-mNeonGreen-Rab11a or/and DExogron-mCherry-Rab11b again showed lower levels of TFN-R recycling compared to control (mainly evident for Rab11a), but tempering expression of Rab11a and Rab11b (or Rab11b alone in DExogron-mCherry-Rab11b cells) by withdrawing dox/adding IAA demonstrated that lower Rab11 levels correlated with increased recycling rates (7C).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Lower Rab11 levels correlated with increased recycling rates.
source: Cells induced to have high-level expression of DExCon-mNeonGreen-Rab11a or/and DExogron-mCherry-Rab11b again showed lower levels of TFN-R recycling compared to control (mainly evident for Rab11a), but tempering expression of Rab11a and Rab11b (or Rab11b alone in DExogron-mCherry-Rab11b cells) by withdrawing dox/adding IAA demonstrated that lower Rab11 levels correlated with increased recycling rates (7C).
evidence: This describes experimental observations.

claim: Competition between fast and slow recycling likely controlled by Rab4 and Rab11a/b, respectively, underpins the differences in recycling rates induced by increasing Rab11 expression level.
source: These data further support the notion that competition between fast and slow recycling likely controlled by Rab4 and Rab11a/b, respectively, underpins the differences in recycling rates induced by increasing Rab11 expression level.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: The DExCon/DExogron system affords control over the timing and level of gene expression of Rab11 family members.
source: Taken together, this suggests that the DExCon/DExogron system affords control over the timing and level of gene expression of Rab11 family members, and points toward a more complex relationship between fast Rab11-independent and slow Rab11-dependent recycling.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on the experimental results.

claim: There is a more complex relationship between fast Rab11-independent and slow Rab11-dependent recycling.
source: Taken together, this suggests that the DExCon/DExogron system affords control over the timing and level of gene expression of Rab11 family members, and points toward a more complex relationship between fast Rab11-independent and slow Rab11-dependent recycling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observations.
